question: There are no Mobium release binaries yet. What do I need on my Mac to install the mobium command, and what is the command?

facts.fact: Until the first release mobium installs with Go 1.24 or later and needs nothing else.
The install command is go install github.com/mobiumdev/mobium/cmd/mobium@latest.
The binary lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin, which must be on PATH.

check: Claude's reading: go.mod declares go 1.24.0, matching the quick start's Go 1.24 or later; cmd/mobium is the main package. SETUP.md#installing-a-release covers the future prebuilt route and is a likely near miss, not gold.

question: I made an Android virtual device in Android Studio. How do I get Mobium to start it and wait until it is ready, and how do I see its screen while it runs?

facts.fact: mobium boot <avd> starts the emulator by its AVD name and answers once Android has finished booting, not merely once adb sees it.
It runs headless unless --window is added.

check: Claude's reading: BootEmulator passes -no-window -no-audio unless window is set (boot.go:139-141) and waits for sys.boot_completed=1 (boot.go:189). SETUP.md#android-emulator says the same in one sentence and may be returned instead; the quick-start section is the fuller answer.

question: My Android emulator won't start and says 'Cannot find valid sdk root path', yet adb works fine from my terminal. What is actually wrong?

facts.fact: platform-tools must be installed into the SDK root by sdkmanager, not only as the Homebrew android-platform-tools cask; the emulator validates the SDK root by that directory.
mobium doctor checks for this specifically.

check: Claude's reading: doctor's android sdk root check fails when the SDK root has no platform-tools directory and says to run sdkmanager platform-tools (doctor.go:115-118). The same trap is named in the doctor command's help text.

question: I restarted my Android emulator and my app came back as a build from days ago, missing screens I added since. Why, and how do I restart it without that happening?

facts.fact: -no-snapshot-save still loads the quick-boot snapshot on the next start, so everything installed since the snapshot is gone.
Cold-boot with -no-snapshot-load, which mobium boot passes, or reinstall what you need and confirm its version.

check: Claude's reading: BootEmulator always passes -no-snapshot-load and its comment cites the old-app snapshot problem (boot.go:116-118, 139). The fact is in part ~1 of the section.

question: What do I have to switch on, on the iPhone itself, before Mobium can drive it?

facts.fact: Trust the computer over a cable and let Xcode's Devices and Simulators window prepare the phone, then turn on Developer Mode.
Turn on Settings > Developer > Enable UI Automation; without it WebDriverAgent fails with "Timed out while enabling automation mode".
Set Auto-Lock to Never (or long enough) so the phone does not lock mid-run.

check: Claude's reading: wdaphone.go recognizes WebDriverAgent's "Timed out while enabling automation mode" log and names the switch (lines 653-660). README.md#platforms~1 lists Developer Mode and Enable UI Automation too and is a plausible near miss, but lacks the trust/Xcode/Auto-Lock steps.

question: Which simulator features does Mobium refuse on a real iPhone, and how do I reset an app's data on a phone instead?

facts.fact: On a phone Mobium refuses permissions, appearance, the clipboard, simulated location and routes, and notifications, each with the reason, because simctl does them and devicectl has no equivalent.
Clearing an app's data on a phone takes its bundle: mobium clear-data <app> --bundle uninstalls and reinstalls the app.

check: Claude's reading: simulatorOnly in wdaphone.go lists exactly permissions, appearance, clipboard read/write, geolocation, routes, clear-data and notifications, and phoneRemedies gives the --bundle reinstall route for clear-data. The code also lists clipboard read separately; the doc says 'the clipboard'.

question: Can I use Mobium on a Windows PC for my Android and iOS app testing today, and how far does that go?

facts.fact: Since 2026-10-22 an Android emulator and a phone have been driven from a Windows laptop through mobium mcp, the CLI and all five clients, but Windows is not yet declared supported.
iOS is not possible on Windows: Mobium drives iOS through xcrun simctl and WebDriverAgent built with Xcode, which is macOS-only.
What is left before support is the checks a person at the machine runs and seven checks whose failures are not yet explained.

concern: docs/quickstart/README.md#where-it-runs still says no emulator or phone has been driven from Windows, which README.md and WINDOWS.md contradict since #270/#271; the quick-start table is stale.
check: Claude's reading: Windows-specific code (named-pipe daemon, Detach, process path) is in internal/device/*_windows.go and builds for windows/amd64; iOS paths call xcrun throughout internal/device. README.md#platforms~2 restates the status in brief and will likely be retrieved; the stale quick-start table is a hard negative.

question: In Git Bash on Windows, pushing a file to /data/local/tmp on my Android device fails because Mobium sees the path as 'C:/Program Files/Git/data/local/tmp/x'. How do I fix it?

facts.fact: Git Bash rewrites any argument that starts with / into a path under Git's own folder before mobium sees it, and Mobium refuses such a path naming the rewrite.
Set MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL="/data/;/sdcard/" to leave device paths alone (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 stops every conversion), or run from PowerShell or cmd, which never rewrite.

check: Claude's reading: CheckDevicePath refuses a path starting with a drive letter as a Git Bash rewrite and its remedy names MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL, MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and PowerShell or cmd (paths.go:126-135). CHALLENGES#361 tells the same story and is a near-equal answer.

question: On Windows, does a Mobium daemon that started inside an SSH session keep running after I disconnect, and what makes that work?

facts.fact: Windows' OpenSSH server kills every process in a session's job when the session ends, which used to take the daemon with it.
Detach now adds CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB when the job allows breakaway, so the daemon outlives the session.

check: Claude's reading: Detach sets CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP|DETACHED_PROCESS and adds CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB only when JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK is set (detach_windows.go:21-40); the auto-started daemon goes through it (daemon_client.go:119). CHALLENGES#359 is the defect behind it and an equally good source.

question: My Android emulator on a Windows host has frozen: adb still lists it but every shell call times out. Will mobium shutdown end it, and how?

facts.fact: mobium shutdown gives adb emu kill ten seconds, then ends the process the emulator's discovery file names once that process is an emulator by name.
On Windows this now works too: the process is read with QueryFullProcessImageName and ended, where it used to be refused.

concern: docs/SHUTDOWN.md#2-simulators-then-emulators still ends with 'On Windows it does not end the process, and says so', but #268 (CHALLENGES 360) made killEmulatorProcess work on Windows (boot.go:400-428, procpath_windows.go); SHUTDOWN.md is stale.
check: Claude's reading: emuKillWait is 10s (boot.go:32) and killEmulatorProcess ends the discovery file's pid when its image name contains qemu or emulator, on every OS (boot.go:400-428). The SHUTDOWN.md section gives the mechanism and CHALLENGES 360 gives Windows; a right answer must say it works on Windows despite the stale line.

question: I run two Android emulators at once on one machine and want a test run on each in parallel without the two slowing each other down. How do I set that up?

facts.fact: With two devices ready, a call that names no device is refused, so each run names its device with --device (or the client's device option); a second emulator gets its own console port with -port 5556.
Give each run its own daemon by naming it with MOBIUM_SESSION, since one daemon serves one call at a time across every device it holds.
Keep the session name short: it is part of a socket path capped at about 104 bytes.

check: Claude's reading: adb.go:429 refuses with 'N devices are ready — pick one with --device'; the daemon serializes handlers with one mutex (daemon.go:30); paths.go names the socket from MOBIUM_SESSION and guards the 104-byte limit. docs/guides/cli.md#8 also explains MOBIUM_SESSION and is a near miss.

question: If I leave Mobium alone for a while, does the background process it started keep running forever?

facts.fact: The first command starts a daemon in the background that holds the device sessions and refs, and it exits after 30 idle minutes.
mobium daemon stop stops it, ending its sessions.

check: Claude's reading: the auto-start passes --idle-timeout 30m (daemon_client.go:19, 114) and watchIdle shuts the daemon down after that (daemon.go:184-210). The question avoids the word daemon on purpose.

question: I have two lab Macs with emulators on them. How do I spread my test runs across both machines' devices, and what does each lab Mac need for that?

facts.fact: Set MOBIUM_GRID=node1,node2; at a run's first call mobium asks each node for its devices and takes the first free one that matches.
Each node needs key-based SSH with no prompt (mobium runs SSH with BatchMode=yes) and mobium reachable by its non-interactive shell, set with MOBIUM_REMOTE_BIN if needed.
On a Mac node, Remote Login must be on.

check: Claude's reading: grid.go splits MOBIUM_GRID on commas and remote.go adds -o BatchMode=yes and honors MOBIUM_SSH and MOBIUM_REMOTE_BIN. SETUP.md#a-grid and SETUP.md#driving-another-machines-devices say most of this too; Remote Login is only in the grid guide.

question: A teammate's phone is plugged into one of our grid machines. Could a grid test run end up installing and tapping on it?

facts.fact: The grid lends a physical device only when the node's own environment sets MOBIUM_GRID_PHONES=1, the node's choice, never the caller's; until then it is listed as not offered.
A grid shows a phone's model, never its name.

check: Claude's reading: grid.go marks a device Offered only if it is an emulator/simulator or the node's MOBIUM_GRID_PHONES is 1 (line 96) and tells a run asking for one so (line 211). SETUP.md#a-grid~1 also covers phones but not the model-not-name point.

question: How do I connect my Fire TV so Mobium can drive it over Wi-Fi from my Mac, and what do I do when adb connect says "No route to host" although the TV answers ping?

facts.fact: Turn on ADB Debugging in the Fire TV's Developer Options (shown under Settings > Device & Software after selecting the device name seven times in About), then run adb connect <tv>:5555 with the TV's IPv4 address and accept the prompt on the TV; a Fire TV has no pairing step.

"No route to host" while ping works is macOS Local Network privacy silently blocking an adb server that a background process started; run adb kill-server && adb connect <tv>:5555 from a Terminal window so macOS asks, and allow it.

check: Claude's reading: replaces a draft that duplicated g074 (simulator audio setup). Both facts are in SETUP.md#over-wi-fi; the Local Network trap is macOS behavior, measured on the Fire TV and recorded in the doc, not something the code can show, and the code's own part is the disconnect-then-connect before it reports a network device missing (internal/device/adb.go:358). SHUTDOWN.md's TV section repeats the trap and could also count.

question: How do I set up an Apple TV simulator for Mobium, and how do I move around in it given that it has no touch screen?

facts.fact: The tvOS platform is a separate download: xcodebuild -downloadPlatform tvOS, then create and boot an Apple TV simulator; the first command installs WebDriverAgent's tvOS runner.
It is driven with the remote: press dpad-up/down/left/right and select, back is the Menu button; tap and other gestures are refused.

check: Claude's reading: remote.go and alerts.go refuse touches on an Apple TV because it has no touch screen, and buttons.go maps back to the remote's Menu button on tvOS. README.md#platforms~2 summarizes TVs and is a near miss without the setup commands.

question: Does Mobium work with Wear OS watches, and what can't it do on one yet?

facts.fact: Wear OS is driven by the Android backends with nothing added, verified on a Wear OS 5.1 emulator, with swiping right as a watch's back.
Not yet a real watch, and not the crown: press has no rotary input.

check: Claude's reading: the press button list in schema.go has D-pad, select, back and media keys and no rotary or crown input; nothing in internal/ handles a crown. SETUP.md#a-wear-os-emulator says 'the crown has no command yet' but not that a real watch is untested, so README is the sufficient section.

question: mobium doctor printed several 'note' lines on my machine. Does that mean my setup is broken, and will doctor fail a CI setup step because of them?

facts.fact: A note means something is missing that is only needed for part of the job, such as no Xcode on a machine doing Android work, which is normal.
doctor checks the whole list without a device and exits non-zero when it found a problem (a FAIL line), so a script can act on it.

check: Claude's reading: only checks with status problem (printed FAIL) count toward Problems, and the command exits non-zero only when Problems > 0, so notes alone exit zero. The doc says 'exits non-zero if it found something', which a reviewer may find vaguer than the code; the answer that notes do not fail is from the code, so the second fact is left to the judge on that point.

question: How do I set up the Mobium daemon to start automatically at login as a launchd or systemd service, so it is always up before my tests run?
check: Claude's reading: the corpus mentions launchd only for simulator internals and Chrome's crash handler, never systemd or a login service; the code only auto-starts the daemon from the first command (daemon_client.go) or `daemon start`. The docs explain auto-start and idle exit, which a retriever will return, but never how to run it as a service.

question: When will Mobium's first prebuilt release, v0.1.0, be published so I can install without Go?
check: Claude's reading: the corpus describes what a release will contain and that installs need Go until the first release, and uses v0.1.0 as an example version, but states no date; release gating is a checklist, not a schedule. A right answer says the docs give no date.

question: My locator text=Settings also clicks things like "Display settings" because it matches part of the text. How do I make a Mobium locator match only an element whose text is exactly Settings?

facts.fact: An unquoted string locator matches part of the words, in any case; putting the value in double quotes matches the whole of it (still in any case).
For example text="Internet" finds only an element whose text is Internet, not "Network & internet".

check: Claude's reading: cli.md section 4 states the quoted-whole rule; Locator.field compares a quoted (Whole) value with strings.EqualFold after trimming, and an unquoted one by case-insensitive substring (match). Reviewer: the question's example is mine, the anchor example is the doc's.

question: Every row in my list has its own "More" button. How do I write a locator in a test file for the More button in the row titled "Card 8", one that still works after the list scrolls?

facts.fact: Use within to scope a locator to a row, e.g. label=More within text=Card 8; both sides are whole locators.
It keeps the match nearest the anchor and never reaches past the list holding the anchor, so a row without the target finds nothing rather than the neighbor's.
Both sides are resolved again on every read, since a list reuses its rows as it scrolls (unlike a ref, which is gone with its map).

check: Claude's reading: cli.md section 4 describes within; Locator.Resolve keeps the target matches nearest the anchor and the comment above it says the climb stops at a scroll container and resolves whole on every read. Facts 2 and 3 have no distinctive token and are left to the judge.

question: In my hybrid app the Save button sits inside an iframe on the embedded web page. How do I tap it from the Mobium CLI?

facts.fact: Switch to the WebView's context first (mobium contexts, then mobium context WEBVIEW_...), after which map and tap operate on the page.
Then use a css= locator with the frame's path before the selector, separated by >>, as map prints it, e.g. 'css=iframe#f >> button'.

check: Claude's reading: README's hybrid section gives the context switch, cli.md section 4 the css= selector with a frame path; findWebByLocator and webview/css.go split the selector on ' >> ' and resolve inside that frame. CHALLENGES 312 and SKILL 'When things fail' also mention the frame path; I kept gold to the two sections a new user needs.

question: Is there a way to click an element on my device's screen and see which locator I should put in my test for it?

facts.fact: Run mobium inspect (optionally --device and --open), which serves a local page showing the device's screen.
Clicking an element shows what map says of it, and at the top the locator a test should use: the most durable one that names it alone (the ref names it on this screen only).
anchors: the locator a test should use

check: Claude's reading: inspector guide sections 1 and 2 together answer it; cmd/mobium/inspect.go defines --port, --open and --record, and inspect.go's target() returns map's derived locator as the one a test names. Section 3 (Try a locator) is related but not needed.

question: On an Apple TV simulator mobium tap is refused. How do I get to a particular tile and open it, and how do I know which tile will be opened before I press?

facts.fact: An Apple TV has no touch screen, so tap and other gestures are refused; it is driven with the remote: press dpad-up/down/left/right to move focus, and press select to press what has focus.
map marks the element with focus as (button, focused), and map --diff reports focus moving, so the focused tile is the one select will press.

check: Claude's reading: SETUP's Apple TV section gives the remote buttons and the refusal of tap; CHALLENGES 355 (#259, after the pin) adds focused to map and map --diff, which snapshot.go and mapdiff.go implement. ROADMAP 'Under consideration' also mentions 355 for the Fire TV.

question: My Compose screen has a Material 3 RangeSlider for a price range, with a minimum and a maximum thumb. How do I set each thumb with Mobium, and how does Mobium move it?

facts.fact: Each thumb is its own slider element (Material reports them as seek bars such as "Range start" and "Range end"), filled one at a time with fill and a position.

A thumb of a two-thumb range is filled by dragging the thumb itself (a touch on the track would move the nearer thumb), and the result is read back from the thumb's own bounds, a short drag corrected.
On Android the drag takes hold 32dp in from the screen's sides (20 points on iOS), so it is not taken as the system back gesture.

check: Claude's reading: CHALLENGES 357 (#262, after the pin) is the only place the native two-thumb fill is described; RangeThumb recognizes two slider/adjustable children of one parent and dragThumb drags and reads back with up to three attempts. The 0-to-1 position rule itself is in CHALLENGES 219 and the fill help, not in 357; I did not make it a fact.

question: After tapping Log In, my test needs to wait until the error label says exactly "Incorrect username or password." How do I write that wait with Mobium, and how long does it wait before failing?

facts.fact: mobium wait <locator> --for text --text "..." --exact waits until the element's text is exactly that (without --exact it waits for the text to contain it).
The default timeout is 10 seconds; --timeout changes it, up to two minutes.

check: Claude's reading: autowait.md section 5 has the exact command and the timeout table; wait.go sets defaultWaitTimeout 10s and maxWaitTimeout 120s, and the CLI's --exact matches the whole text. The 10-second and two-minute numbers are too common in the corpus to anchor, so fact 2 is left to the judge.

question: What does Mobium do when I tap a button that another view is drawn over, both when the cover hides the whole button and when it hides only the middle of it?

facts.fact: Fully covered: it waits about two seconds in case the cover goes (a toast does), then refuses with failed check receivesEvents, naming the cover, rather than pressing it.
Covered only over its center: it taps a clear point of the target and says so in the result.

check: Claude's reading: autowait.md section 3 shows both outputs; resolveAim waits up to the implicit wait (2s; longer for a notification banner) for a full cover, then coveredBy refuses, and a center-only cover gets the 'touched at a clear point' note.

question: How long will a Mobium tap keep waiting for a button that is still animating into place, and how long for one that is disabled, before it gives up?

facts.fact: The stable check waits up to 5 seconds for the target to stop moving, then refuses.
The enabled check waits up to the implicit wait of 2 seconds for the control to take input, then refuses.

concern: skills/mobile-check/SKILL.md#acting says every action waits 'for up to two seconds, until its target is on screen, enabled and holding still'; the code's settleTimeout for holding still is 5 seconds (internal/agent/wait.go:47), as autowait.md says. The skill's sentence understates the stable wait.
check: Claude's reading: autowait.md's checks table matches wait.go (implicitWait 2s, settleTimeout 5s) and the enabled poll in resolveNodeOnce uses h.implicitWait. The skill's 'up to two seconds' for all three is the disagreement in concern. The numbers are too common to anchor; the anchors are the check names, and the judge must hold 5 s and 2 s.

question: After mobium press back on Android, how can my test tell whether the app went to its previous screen or closed altogether?

facts.fact: press back says what back did: 'it left <app>; <app> is in the foreground' when back left the app, or '<app> is still in the foreground' when it stayed inside it.

check: Claude's reading: BACK.md 'In Mobium' lists the outcome wording; backOutcome in back.go builds exactly those strings. SKILL 'Interruptions and hardware buttons' says the same; I kept gold to BACK.md, so a reviewer may want to add the skill section as an alternative.

question: My CI script needs to tell a tap refused because something covered the target apart from other failures. What exit status and JSON fields should it check?

facts.fact: With --json the refusal has code element_not_reachable, and the CLI exits with status 4.
details.check names the failed check (receivesEvents for a cover); decide by code and details.check, never by the message text, which may change.

check: Claude's reading: autowait.md section 6 shows the JSON and names exit 4; mobiumerr.ExitCode returns 4 for element_not_reachable and failedCheck puts check and reason in details. Exit 4 also covers no_such_element and ambiguous_locator, so the code field is what separates them.

question: In my Compose app the Price filter chip is off the right edge of a horizontal row of chips that sits above a large product grid. Which container does mobium scroll-to --direction right swipe to find it?

facts.fact: A scroll given a direction swipes the largest scrollable whose class says it scrolls that way; Compose reports a horizontalScroll row as HorizontalScrollView, so the chip row is swiped, not the grid.
An up or down scroll never swipes a row that says it scrolls sideways; nothing infers an axis that no class states.

concern: skills/mobile-check/SKILL.md#reaching-things-below-the-fold says scroll-to is for 'Vertical lists only. For a horizontal pager or carousel use mobium swipe left', but scroll-to takes --direction left/right (cmd/mobium/scroll.go:17 and :27, example 'a horizontal pager') and scrollContainerFor picks a sideways row (internal/agent/scroll.go:893). The skill is stale.
check: Claude's reading: CHALLENGES 358 (#262, after the pin) is the only description; scrollContainerFor in scroll.go matches it line for line. The skill's 'vertical lists only' contradicts the code; see concern.

question: mobium press back --gesture is refused on my Android emulator, while plain press back works. Why, and how do I check which mode the device is in?

facts.fact: An edge swipe is back only in gesture navigation; with three-button navigation it does nothing, so press back --gesture is refused there and the back button (plain press back) is the user's back.
The mode can be read with settings get secure navigation_mode (2 gestures, 0 three buttons), and mobium devices names an Android device's navigation mode.

check: Claude's reading: BACK.md 'MobiumApp as shipped' measured that edge swipes do nothing in three-button mode and gives navigation_mode values; 'In Mobium' says --gesture is refused on button navigation and devices names the mode. gestureBack returns unsupported unless the mode is gestures.

question: mobium contexts lists only NATIVE_APP for my app even though a screen clearly shows web content. Why can't Mobium see the WebView, and what has to change?

facts.fact: A WebView is reachable only if the app opted in: WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) on Android, isInspectable on iOS 16.4 and later; neither can be forced from outside.

check: Claude's reading: README's hybrid section states the opt-in; noWebViewsHint gives the same remedy per platform when contexts finds none, and adds that a page must be open on iOS. SKILL 'Hybrid apps' repeats it; gold kept to README.

question: On an iPhone, my tap on Add to Cart is refused because the on-screen keyboard covers the button. How do I get the keyboard out of the way?

facts.fact: On an iPhone, which has no hide key, use mobium keyboard --key enter; elsewhere mobium keyboard --hide.

check: Claude's reading: the skill's receivesEvents bullet gives both commands; handlers.go's hideKeyboard remedy text says the same, naming the iPhone's missing hide key. CHALLENGES 325 shows keyboard --key enter working on a simulator but is not needed.

question: Can Mobium move the two thumbs of a range slider in an Android app built with Views, using the Material Components RangeSlider rather than Compose?

facts.fact: Native two-thumb sliders are done for Material 3's RangeSlider in Compose and an iOS app's own (since 2026-10-22); a View-system RangeSlider (Material Components) is not yet supported, nor measured on a phone.

check: Claude's reading: ROADMAP 'Under consideration', Sliders entry, says not yet for a View-system RangeSlider; RangeThumb needs two slider children under one parent, which the Compose and iOS builds give — a View RangeSlider is one view, so it would not be recognized. That last point is my reading of the code, not measured.

question: Why does mobium tap @e5 look the element up again instead of tapping the coordinates that mobium map printed for it?

facts.fact: tap re-snapshots and re-resolves the ref's locator before touching anything.
It never replays map's coordinates because the screen moves between commands, and a tap at a stale point fails silently; a locator that became ambiguous is refused rather than guessed.

check: Claude's reading: README 'Refs' gives the reason; the comment on resolveNode says every action re-snapshots, since acting on a node from an older snapshot lands on whatever moved into its place.

question: Why does Mobium refuse press-tap (hold one finger, then tap with a second) on an iPhone instead of just sending it?

facts.fact: XCTest (through WebDriverAgent) gives a finger that lands after the gesture began an extra zero-length touch at its target at time zero.

An app can read that instant touch as a tap before the gesture, so Mobium refuses press-tap and press-drag on iOS rather than send a gesture that is also something else; multi-finger taps are unaffected.

check: Claude's reading: GESTURES.md 'Three ways a second finger went wrong' explains it; errLateFinger in multitouch.go carries the same reason. Android 16+ is refused for a different reason (UiAutomator2's down time), in the same section's second part — not asked here.

question: How do I raise Mobium's implicit wait so every tap waits up to 10 seconds for its target instead of 2?
check: Claude's reading: the docs state the 2-second implicit wait but never say whether it can be changed; no flag, env var or argument sets it — implicitWait is a constant (wait.go:32) whose comment says longer waits belong in an explicit wait. A retriever will return the checks table and mobium wait's --timeout, which answers a different question.

question: How long does mobium long-press hold the press by default when I don't pass --duration?
check: Claude's reading: the default is 800ms in code (CLI flag and app_long_press's duration_ms), but no corpus section states it; GESTURES only says a 50ms hold must read as a tap, and FLAGS lists --duration without a default. CHALLENGES 86 mentions --lead-ms 800 for press-tap, a likely false match.

question: I recorded a flow in mobium inspect. How do I get it as a Python program instead of a .test.json file, and which device will that program drive?

facts.fact: Next to Download in the inspector, pick the language: the test file, or a program in Python, JavaScript, Go, Java or .NET.
The program starts from the app launched fresh (terminated, then launched), as mobium test starts each test.
The program names no device: start() takes the only one running, and start(device=...) names one.

check: Claude's reading: inspector.md section 5 (added in #261, after 7b590a4) answers all three; codegen.Program prepends app_terminate and app_launch, and the Python writer emits `with start() as device:`. The device-selection part comes from the same section, so the question stays a single fact.

question: While I click through my app in the inspector, how can I have the recording written into a file in my project as it grows, and which kinds of file can it write?

facts.fact: mobium inspect --record <file> writes the recording after every step.
The file is a .test.json, or a program chosen by its extension: .py, .mjs, .go, .java or .cs, the same file the download gives.

check: Claude's reading: the --record paragraph sits at the end of inspector.md section 4, not section 5, which is why the gold is #4; the extension table in codegen.go matches the doc's five. New since the pin (#261).

question: My inspector recording includes a two-finger tap. What happens when I try to download it as a Go program?

facts.fact: A step the language table cannot write exactly, such as a two-finger tap or a wait for a count, is refused when you download, naming the step, rather than written as a different step.
For such a recording, download the test file instead.

check: Claude's reading: codegen.unsupported returns an unsupported error "step N (...) cannot be written as code" with the remedy "download the recording as a test file and run it with mobium test", matching the doc. question: With Mobium's Python client, how do I make sure the device session is ended even when my script raises an exception partway?

facts.fact: Use `with start(...) as device:`, which quits when the block ends, even on an exception.
Without `with`, call `device.quit()` yourself in a `finally`.

check: Claude's reading: Device.__exit__ calls quit() for a device from start() and only close() for one from connect(); quit() is idempotent, so an explicit quit plus a with block is fine.

question: The .NET client is not on NuGet yet. How do I add it to my project?

facts.fact: Clone the repository and build a local package with `dotnet pack` from clients/dotnet/Mobium into a folder.
Add it with `dotnet add package Mobium --version 0.1.0 --source <that folder>`.

check: Claude's reading: the csproj's PackageId is Mobium and Version 0.1.0, matching the quickstart's `--version 0.1.0`.

question: Why would a pull request that adds a separate implementation of some behavior just for the MCP server be pushed back on in Mobium?

facts.fact: Mobium's design rule, mutatis mutandis, is to carry the existing thing with only the necessary changes, not a parallel implementation; a change that duplicates a layer is almost always the wrong one.
Behavior lives in internal/agent and the CLI only parses flags and calls a tool by name, so the MCP surface and every client get it too.

check: Claude's reading: CONTRIBUTING's design rule says both; the code matches — `mobium mcp` serves agent.NewServer, the same tool layer the daemon dispatches to, and apisurface fails the build on drift between front doors.

question: I'm driving a real Android phone on the office Wi-Fi with Mobium's default driver. Can others on that network get at the phone while my session is open, and what does Mobium offer instead?

facts.fact: Yes: the session's answer says the UiAutomator2 server answers on the phone's network until the session ends.
It names `--driver uiautomator`, which drives the phone through `uiautomator dump` over adb and listens on nothing.

check: Claude's reading: sessionExposure returns the warning only for the uiautomator2 backend on a non-emulator device; its text also says the uiautomator driver reads at about 2 s a screen and cannot type, which this section does not mention.

question: The MCP guide shows `tools/list` answering 71 tools, but `mobium mcp` lists 75 for me. Is my install wrong?

facts.fact: No: the generated tool surface in API.md counts 75 tools today.
The guide's transcripts are from a run on 2026-09-28, and its full tool list is the generated API.md.

concern: docs/guides/mcp.md:126 and :296 and docs/quickstart/mcp.md:134 and :166 still say 71 tools; the code (internal/agent/schema.go) has 75, and API.md said 73 at the pin. The guide and quickstart are stale.
check: Claude's reading: schema.go defines 75 app_ tools; app_speech and app_assistant were added after 7b590a4 (73 at the pin). A right answer needs API.md for the count and the guide's intro for why its number is older.

question: My driver should let Mobium scroll and use scroll-to. What do I have to advertise and implement?

facts.fact: Advertise the `gestures` capability in the initialize reply; it unlocks scrolling, scroll-to and long press.
Implement `swipe` taking x1, y1, x2, y2 and durationMs (and `longPress` taking x, y, durationMs), in device pixels.

check: Claude's reading: README's capabilities table maps gestures to swipe and longPress and what they unlock; PROTOCOL's methods table has the parameters, which External.Swipe and LongPress send exactly.

question: I want two agents, each driving its own Android emulator through Mobium's MCP server at the same time. How do I set them up so they don't get in each other's way?

facts.fact: Pin each server to its own device, e.g. `mobium mcp --device emulator-5554` in each client's configuration.
Each `mobium mcp` runs the tools in its own process with its own device sessions, and a device's automation server holds one session at a time, so each agent needs its own device.

check: Claude's reading: SetDefaultDevice is set from the global --device in mcp_cmd.go; that two servers on two different devices work together is implied by section 6 rather than stated as a run, which a reviewer may want to weigh.

question: Can I put Mobium into a read-only mode so my agent can look at the screen but never act on the device?

facts.fact: Not in Mobium itself: a read-only mode Mobium enforces, and a tool allowlist, are listed as open.
Every MCP tool carries `readOnlyHint`, true only for the tools that only read (`app_map`, `app_text`, `app_state` and the like), so the agent's harness can allow only reads.

check: Claude's reading: readonly.go lists 19 read-only tools and schema.go sets readOnlyHint from it; `mobium mcp` has no read-only flag. Unrelated defect seen while checking: app_network's new `proxy` argument is missing from readUnless in readonly.go, so IsReadCall treats a proxy-setting call as a read for the test runner's expect.

question: How many tool calls per minute will Mobium's MCP server accept before it starts throttling my agent?
check: Claude's reading: no rate limit is stated anywhere in the corpus, and the code has none (grep for rate limit or throttle in internal/agent and cmd/mobium finds only Android's crash-record limit); the threat model's unbounded-consumption row lists per-call timeouts, batches of at most 100 steps and backgrounding of at most 180 s, which a retriever will bring back.

question: When will Mobium's Python client be published on PyPI so I can just run pip install mobium?
check: Claude's reading: the quickstart says only that `pip install mobium` works after the first release, and the roadmap lists the registry accounts to set up; no date for the first release or the PyPI publish is given anywhere in the corpus.
